steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Welcome to Teatro di Milano, signorine mie.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Wow, this place is breathtaking!

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Siracusans love to kill time here to the accompaniment of music and performance. After all, when reality is monotonous and difficult to change, people naturally need a place to indulge their fantasies.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Or, to equate their bloodstained business dealings with the legendary exploits of the heroes on stage to obtain a sense of moral satisfaction.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Wow... you really don't pull any punches, huh?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Of course not. In this line of work, we must be clear-eyed about our own profession, no?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Your friends over there seem to have been on their guard from the very beginning.

steps.name: Croissant
steps.text: I don't mean no disrespect, Mr. Director, but the way I heard it, you was callin' that play yer rehearsin'...

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: 'La Morte di Texas.'

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: 'The Death of Texas'? That might be the crappiest 'joke' I've ever heard.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Hm? You seem to be well-acquainted with that name. That's fairly unusual among foreigners.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Siracusans rarely bring it up in the first place, and the mafiosi here are even more secretive about it. But the story of Famiglia Texas... is one that every mafioso must always keep in their hearts.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: It is a cautionary tale.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: A warning...

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Let's talk about the script itself first. There are countless works based on the deeds of Famiglia Texas, but not a single one dares to actually print the name.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Playwrights are more inclined to reimagine or adapt, with the help of allusion or parody. After all, it is against their interests to invite trouble.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: However, times change, and today's audience finds true history far more salient than fairy tales with falsified names. Wouldn't you agree?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: As such, a remarkable individual has brought this script before us.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: It's a play in three acts.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: The first act harkens back to the era when Columbia was first established, with many a Siracusan famiglia yearning for this undeveloped land.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Consequently, the famiglie each dispatched their own teams, one after another, joining the ranks of Columbia's first pioneers.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: 'In an era when chaos and opportunity came hand-in-hand, some were swallowed by the tides of the times, while others found in it their promised land.'

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: The cream of the crop among them was Salvadore Texas, a man who would later establish his very own era.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: (I know he means the surname and not her, but still...)

spans.text: (I know he means the surname and not

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: So, Texas is one of Siracusa's families?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: To be precise, they were a famiglia that originated in Siracusa, but took root in Columbia.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Such famiglie are hardly unusual over there.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: From beginning to end, though, old Salvadore saw himself as a Siracusan, through-and-through.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: And the Siracusans in turn rewarded him for his perseverance, always affording him a Siracusan's respect.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: The Siracusans...

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: The second act chronicles some of the most praiseworthy episodes from his storied struggles in Columbia.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Siracusans can be found everywhere in the shadows of Columbia's history, and it is precisely amidst that tide that Salvadore gathered his famiglia.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: In truth, the contents of this act are the best known of the three.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Even across various retellings, they're almost always the same.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Accounts of 'the Siracusan in Columbia' can be found in over a dozen versions in any local bookstore, mostly romance novels borrowing the phantom of his name, so to speak.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Perhaps, there may even be a few words of truth among them.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: If you're interested in that, I can point you to some of the less-outrageous ones.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Ooh, I'd appreciate that!

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Think nothing of it. Now, onto the third act - this is the one that can change most dramatically between versions.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Because... it deals with the fall of the Texas Family?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: That's right.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Outsiders only know one thing for certain about the fall of Famiglia Texas, and that is that—

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Salvadore was murdered by his own son, Giuseppe, who later declared that Famiglia Texas would break away from Siracusa's famiglia system.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: This act angered Signora Sicilia, and incurred her retribution.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: In a single night, the Texas name was wiped from existence.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: The entire Texas family disappeared... in a single night?!

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: At least, that's what every Siracusan believes.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: As far as what exactly happened during the liquidation of Famiglia Texas, nobody except the parties involved have any way of knowing.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Excuse me... How come there are only scripts for the first two acts here?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: That is because the third act is not yet finished.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Each playwright will invariably imagine their own version of how this process unfolded, arriving at completely different developments and outcomes.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: In that regard, our playwright seems to have reached an impasse.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: That said, the contents of the first two acts are already exceptional on their own merits, so I purchased the work without hesitation.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Mr. Bernardo, is it possible that one of the heirs of the Texas Family survived the chaos?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Like, maybe she... managed to leave Columbia and escape to a different city?

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: For example... Lungmen?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Lungmen? If I recall, that's where you ladies hail from.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Apparently, Salvadore did not have a particularly amicable relationship with his son.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: But he doted on his granddaughter, even sending her back to Siracusa, where she was fostered by Famiglia Saluzzo for several years.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Nobody has seen or heard from her since the liquidation, though.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: In fact, nobody can conclusively say if she was even involved in this at all. Some say she's been seen in Columbia, or even along the border of Siracusa.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Therefore, different accounts of Famiglia Texas's story tend to have different endings when it comes to her.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: She was said to possess their iconic black hair and orange eyes.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: If—and I'm speaking hypothetically here! If the last descendant of the Texas Family is still alive, and has returned to Siracusan soil once again...

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: What would happen then?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Certainly a thought-provoking hypothetical, one with any number of possible developments. Playwrights tend to build their work around such logic.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Sadly, Signorina Sora, reality does not abide by logic.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Some say that she is the 'guest' of a family by the name of Bellone.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Some say that the Bellones are the most powerful family in the city.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Some say that she...

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Some say that she left everything behind to go there, not even giving herself a chance to say goodbye.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: I, no, we came all the way here to find her.

spans.text: came all the way here to find her.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Your bravery is commendable.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Since you have been so frank with me, bringing secrets even I have never heard, allow me to be frank with you in turn.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Famiglia Bellone and their guests have indeed frequented this theater, graciously offering their patronage to our humble performances.

steps.name: Sora
steps.text: Really?!

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Call it coincidence, or call it fate. Is that not how all stories unfold?

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: If that guest truly comes to pay us a visit, then our troupe will be sure to extend her an enthusiastic welcome.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Rumor has it that she is a woman of few words, whose twin swords speak for her.

steps.name: Bernardo
steps.text: Her name is... Cellinia Texas.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Stop shoving that plate of thistles in my face, Lavinia.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The seasoning here isn't as bad as you make it out to be. Give it a try.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I'm going to have to pass again.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Are you trying to save room in your stomach for a cold dinner with those smug mafiosi friends of yours back home, who reek of cigar butts?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: After all, only the things that happen there have any real 'value.'

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: No... I just seriously can't stand artichokes.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Leon, I've already lost count of the number of violent incidents that have broken out in this city over the past month.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Just this morning, a citizen nearly died at this very restaurant.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You're a judge. You should know better than anyone else that Siracusa was built on violence.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Should there ever come a day when there aren't any unidentifiable corpses lying in the alleys, then that would be real news.

spans.text: Should there ever come a day when there aren't any unidentifiable corpses lying in the alleys, then

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The victim was an employee of il Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici. Your ministero.

spans.text: The victim was an employee of il Ministero dei Lavori Pubblici.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: ...Who did it?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: It would appear that Leontuzzo, son of Don Bellone deigns to inquire about the life and death of a citizen only when it concerns his career.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Your Honor, Lavinia Falcone, I really do not have the energy to clap back at you right now.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: We can all feel that this city has been on edge recently... waiting for something big to happen.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Something bigger than the Bellones' ultimate victory?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: If we really are allowed to take the reins, I, for one, do not intend to continue tolerating the thugs that prowl in the cover of darkness.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Lavinia, you're familiar with the way I do things.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I sure hope so.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Over a hundred years ago, when Siracusa first turned from a plot of land into a country, its territory consisted of the twenty-two cities controlled by the Dodici Famiglie.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And to this day, that number has never changed.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Just like Siracusa's ironclad 'tradition.'

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: But finally, after so many years, our ever-immutable Siracusa is about to give birth to a new nomadic city.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: A new nomadic city means new opportunities, new ambitions, and new hopes. You're exactly right, we are indeed at victory's doorstep.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Economy, traffic, and route planning. We and our friends have already been spreading our influence through every facet of Volsinii's new urban area.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: When that area is formally built into a new city, we will have the right to lead the future of Siracusa. At least, that's what the more optimistic associates of the famiglia believe.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: And do you consider yourself one of those optimists?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I very much hope I am.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That said, the old fellas over at Grey Hall haven't reached their final decision yet.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: There's no future to look forward to until everyone there has formally let the chips fall.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Are we still looking forward to the same future, Leon?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: ...Of course.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Alright, it's about time for me to head off.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Before the banquet starts, I have to first pick up a certain... 'friend.'

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: This whole city is sopping wet.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Sorry to keep you waiting.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I was just looking around.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Celli... Signorina Texas, how do you feel about the way your hometown has changed?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: These newfangled streets and alleys? That hardly counts as 'change.'

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: The way I see it, it's exactly the same as the day I left.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: And... this outfit. I don't think it's a very good idea.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Consider it your very first gift from Famiglia Bellone. Hopefully, you'll find that our tailor has not besmirched the former glory of Famiglia Texas. Please, be at ease and accept it.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: So if I'm not at ease, can I refuse?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Unfortunately, I'm afraid that is not an option.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Guess I'll have to find a way to ease up then.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: So, what's my job here?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: It's very simple - you'll join me at tonight's banquet, where I'll proudly announce in front of everyone that I, the son of Don Bellone, have enlisted a bodyguard who's inherited the Texas name.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Then, you'll kill all the overzealous, power-hungry idiots there, and we'll call it a day.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I'd actually be down for that.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Same. If only it were ever that easy.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Alright, Texas. In the two days I've left you in the city, I've been hard at work conditioning my mind.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I've been trying to tell myself that the Texas name is worth a whole lot more than the trouble you're going to bring.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That way, I can gradually come to terms with the terrifyingly dangerous situation I've been dealt.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: The Texases are already dead.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Unfortunately, not everyone believes that.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Maybe you're the one misreading how much influence a ruined famiglia can have.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Maybe, but I'm not just talking about Famiglia Texas here. I'm also talking about you.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You once returned to Siracusa from Columbia, only to leave again.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: The way I heard it, every famiglia involved in the 'liquidation' tried to kill you on your way out, but every last one of them failed.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: They were all made to pay a heavy price, and it was all sparked by a single woman—you.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: I just work for Penguin Logistics. I do deliveries.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: If you've already made your assessment of how much you're worth to Siracusa today, then let me assure you that—

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I know at least as much as you do.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: First things first, Signorina. You must have some idea of what's going on in Volsinii, right?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: ...A new nomadic city.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Precisely.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And regardless of whether you acknowledge it or not, this plan is closely tied to your family name.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Or should I say... it was brought on by the fall of Famiglia Texas.
The collapse of the Texases dealt a mortal blow to the authority of Columbia's famiglie, and they had no choice but to return to Siracusa's embrace.
They brought back Columbian technology as the price for regaining our trust. Finally, Siracusa had acquired the ability to build a new city of its own.
However, the most pressing issue quickly became who would have the rights to own it, and the power struggle within Grey Hall began the moment the plan to build the city was completed five years ago.
Today, that power struggle is finally drawing to a close.
As one of the oldest famiglie, we, the Bellones, have the opportunity to seize victory.
Volsinii's backup core is already being retrofitted to serve as the core of the new city, and new plates are steadily being built.
In a year's time, perhaps even less, it will be completed.
And your mission... is to help Famiglia Bellone turn this opportunity into a decisive victory.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Sounds to me like what you needed was just a good enough hitman.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But when the hitman's name is Texas, that might just change everything.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Do you still remember the Rossati name?

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Rossati...? Yeah, that rings a bell.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: After the Texases were liquidated, the famiglie that had taken root in Columbia lived in constant fear of becoming the next target of Signora Sicilia's wrath.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: That's when Famiglia Rossati took the initiative to approach her themselves. They were the ones who brought back the technology to develop nomadic cities.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: For a brief moment, the Rossatis were poised to succeed the Texases, even managing to squeeze into one of the Twelve Seats of Grey Hall that no Texas had ever touched.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: This seems like one of those boring stories that goes nowhere.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Boring, and brutal. Grey Hall has always been like that - open only to the winners.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: And the boss of Famiglia Rossati stationed in this city, Signor Wallach, will not be content lapping up the scraps we Bellones leave behind.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: And here I was thinking the dour mood around here was because of the rainy season.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I'll be frank with you: Volsinii has not been peaceful these last few months. A few of our friends have found themselves in various kinds of 'accidents.'

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Along with them, the famiglie who still remain on the sidelines may end up changing their minds, and there's no guarantee that the famiglie that have already chosen their alliances won't betray them later.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: When Signora Sicilia established Grey Hall, she laid down an ironclad rule: 'Do not kill.'

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: In other words, the famiglie have a lot of leeway to do whatever they want, short of killing one another.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Could've fooled me.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: You are still standing in front of me, after all.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: And so, you invited me back.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: You don't need me to do anything in particular; I just have to get up on the stage you've prepared and announce that I've returned.

steps.name: Texas
steps.text: And that stage is tonight, correct?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: Signorina Texas, are you aware...

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: ...that the fall of the Texases has been adapted into one opera after another, performed across various major theaters?

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: In those stories, you, Cellinia Texas, are always portrayed as an ignorant child, helpless in the face of your family's collapse.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: But right now, I can say for sure that you are anything but.

steps.name: Leontuzzo
steps.text: I truly want to know... What exactly did you experience during that 'liquidation'?

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: You've returned, Your Honor?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Yes. Is something going on?

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Remember how Alessia said she recently met a pretty nice guy?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The one who runs the textile shop?

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: So you knew after all!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Yes, we've crossed paths a few times back when I was investigating a case. His famiglia...

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Yes, Famiglia Gelli! Though they're not a particularly major famiglia, they still control all the textile businesses for a few streets down!

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: I heard they even have business dealings with some of the famiglie that make their way in and out of Grey Hall!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Yes, we know.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Alessia has been talking us up for ages. She said the guy's going to bring some of his siblings along so we can all have a good time together!

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: It's been so busy around here lately, I haven't had a chance to cut loose and unwind!

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Oh, Your Honor, umm...

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: You... aren't going, right?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Right... I still have some work to do. Tell them I send my regards.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Okay! Will do!

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Oh right, did you get a chance to look through those files?

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Which files?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The mass disappearance on Via Como. Family of five. Remember?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I've located a potential witness and am trying to convince him to testify.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: But, Judge Angelo declared that case closed as of this afternoon.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: He said... He said that family just moved to another city. Then, he added that we still have too many things to do, and shouldn't waste our time and energy on cases like this.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Unless I am misremembering, I am the judge presiding over this case.

spans.text: am the judge presiding over this case.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: The court made the decision internally yesterday. You weren't present for the meeting.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Is that so...?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I get it.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Right, this case is certainly not worth the time and energy. It's only five people after all.

spans.text: not worth the time and energy. It's

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The husband drives a taxi around the city. The wife picks tomatoes on a farm. They have three children, the oldest only thirteen years of age, the youngest still breastfeeding.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: The neighbors were reluctant to say anything, and no matter who I asked, they all said that life must move on.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: There was no screaming in the night, no crying by the lake, and no traces of blood left on their squeaky-clean floorboards.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Alright then. Life must move on, and they had it coming for crossing a famiglia. Or maybe their luck was so rotten they didn't even notice they were being targeted.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: After all, the famiglie always say they would never attack ordinary civilians.

spans.text: After all, the famiglie always say they would

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: And as for us judges, there are always more important things to attend to, right?

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Your Honor, I've always had the greatest respect for you.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: To be honest, I have no idea what an ideal judge is supposed to look like.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Even though the Signora modeled our courts after Laterano's, and codified our laws after Columbia's...

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: None of us have ever seen a real one of Sankta's wandering judges, and Columbia's Code of Law is but an excerpt from a book.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: What I would rather believe is that an ideal judge should be someone as determined to uphold justice as you are.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: But not everyone has your talents, or your connections with Famiglia Bellone. You don't have to constantly fear for your life.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: No, I just—

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: You can casually grab a light meal with the son of the Don.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: And earlier this morning, Judge Angelo received a letter sealed in a black envelope.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...Which famiglia is behind this case?

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Does it make a difference, as far as we're concerned?

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Do you still remember last month how Judge Starocci was dragged by his 'friends' to 'chat' in a car for an entire afternoon? He hasn't been able to lift his right hand since.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Then there's Judge Borriello... That chubby, always-jovial old lady. How long has it been since she came to work?

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: You're right, in theory we're supposed to represent that woman's will. But what is that even supposed to be? At least, I can't figure it out.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Courage and persistence are great things to have, of course, but Judge Lavinia, please do not laugh at the wet clothes of us folks who stand beneath the eaves.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: After all, you have nothing to lose.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Is that so...?

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Perhaps the price I pay... is the right to truly be just.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Oh, the phones here don't ring very often. They usually prefer to come settle things privately.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Or should I say, they look to settle things with us privately.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Hello.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: Got it. I'll be there right away.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Your Honor, you know you don't have to take everything so seriously.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Court Clerk
steps.text: Should I bring back some macaroni for supper? We're going to a restaurant with pretty good reviews.

steps.name: Lavinia
steps.text: ...Appreciate it.
